sourceIssues.printed: “so, by [Gir71, III.3.2.2], the map” H¹_et(V,G) → H¹_et(V,Res_{R′/R}(G_{R′})) “is injective.”
sourceIssues.correction: For full injectivity, restrict Proposition 2.2 to commutative G; this covers both uses, Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.4. Alternatively, retain arbitrary affine smooth G but weaken the conclusion to triviality of the fibre over the trivial torsor. To retain the original full noncommutative statement, supply surjectivity of (^P H)(V) → (^P X)(V) for every G-torsor P over V, where H=Res_{R′/R}(G_{R′}), X=H/G, the groups are twisted by conjugation and X by the induced G-action.
sourceIssues.reason: Affineness gives X(R)=X(V), and H¹(R,G)=1 lifts each X(R)-point to H(R). Thus H(V)→X(V) is surjective. The torsor boundary sequence identifies H(V)\X(V) with only the neutral fibre of H¹(V,G)→H¹(V,H). For a torsor P the fibre through [P] instead identifies with (^P H)(V)\(^P X)(V): twisting sends [P] to the trivial torsor. These twists are initially defined over V, and no extension of them to affine R-schemes is established. If P itself extended, hypothesis (2) would make it trivial, leaving precisely the other fibres untreated. This fibre calculation is also explicit for group cohomology in Serre, Galois Cohomology, I.§5.3 Proposition 35 and §5.4 Proposition 36, Corollaries 1–2, pp.49–51 (the inherited §5.5 Corollary 2 citation was incorrect). If G is commutative, so is H; the H¹ map is a group homomorphism, so its trivial kernel proves injectivity. Proposition 2.3 applies this to the commutative quotient Res(T)/T, and Corollary 2.4 to the torus T. Therefore this gap does not obstruct these applications or their downstream purity arguments. No counterexample to the geometric proposition is asserted.

review.reason: Independently read arXiv v4 §2 (pp.3–6), Proposition 2.2 in a page image and the author manuscript, and Serre I.§5.3–5.5 pp.47–52 as page images. The actual fibre formula is §5.4 Corollary 2, not the inherited §5.5 citation; corrected the report in place. Checked the torsor exactness argument, twists and both commutative uses. An exhaustive C₂-cohomology diagnostic for D₈⊂S₄ has a singleton neutral fibre but merges two nontrivial classes, illustrating the invalid formal implication without claiming a counterexample to this geometric proposition. Added the valid weaker neutral-fibre conclusion as an alternative repair. Confirmed as a proof gap in the two accessible manuscripts; the Duke text and Giraud III.3.2.2 were not accessible and are not certified. No effect on the checked commutative applications.
